name: Gulf / US–Iran war
value: Tankers hit 8 Nov; Trump says strikes unlikely
summary: Trump calls new strikes highly unlikely while talks progress; Iran says tankers burned in Hormuz on 8 Nov
state: President Trump said on 8 Nov that fresh attacks were highly unlikely while talks progress; Foreign Minister Araghchi said the US must accept Iran's two-day proposal or face war, and the Revolutionary Guards said three tankers caught fire in Hormuz that day (The New Arab). Centcom said a US aircraft disabled the M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman on 7 Nov (Euronews). Trump confirmed a US strike on an Iranian air-defence system after explosions on Qeshm on 6 Nov; Iranian agencies reported further blasts on 7 Nov, with no cause stated (Euronews).
for_you: FCDO travel advice covers Iran and the Gulf states and is the reference for anyone travelling or living in the region. Airspace and flight schedules can change at short notice. Crews and operators in the Gulf can follow UKMTO notices.
rubric_hit: Alert: active strikes between states and attacks on Gulf shipping; US disabled M/V Huda on 7 Nov, Iran reports tanker fires on 8 Nov

sources.title: Trump says unlikely to attack Iran, Araghchi warns US on talks
US forces strike commercial vessel in Gulf of Oman after crew 'ignored repeated warnings'

why: Direct hostilities between Iran and the US or Israel threaten Gulf energy infrastructure, the Strait of Hormuz and the wider region.
drivers: Strikes and retaliation, attacks on shipping and Gulf states, mediation and ceasefire talks, US force posture.

rubric.alert: Active strikes between states, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure or shipping, or the Strait of Hormuz substantially closed.
rubric.watch: A ceasefire or stalemate with sporadic strikes, or credible threats of renewed strikes.
rubric.normal: No direct state-on-state hostilities; diplomacy active.
